::: {#bio}
**Remote sensing · Environmental change · Geography**

I’m a **Ph.D. candidate in Geography at UC Santa Barbara**, studying how ecosystems respond to environmental change. I combine active and passive remote sensing data with field observations to understand landscapes across space and time.

My dissertation examines **drought impacts on Southern California oak woodlands**, with a focus on **imaging spectroscopy**. My earlier work used satellite observations and machine learning to quantify fog in Taiwan’s montane cloud forests.

::: {.availability}
**Seeking a summer 2027 internship**

I’m interested in opportunities to apply remote sensing and environmental data analysis to real-world questions. [Get in touch](mailto:hsinjuli@ucsb.edu).
:::

[Explore my research](projects.qmd){.btn .btn-primary} [More about me](about.qmd){.btn .btn-outline-primary}

Outside research, you’ll usually find me climbing, running, or playing board games with friends.
:::
